🧭 How to use this guide

There is one section for each of the 10 Computer lessons. Each one has the big idea, the key words, a picture, every worksheet question of that lesson with its answer, the written answers to learn, a memory trick, a Watch out box and Try these questions (answers at the back). At the end: a one-page cheat sheet and all 25 model answers together.

💡 Memory trickAn easy way to remember.
⚠️ Watch outA mix-up that loses marks.
✏️ Try thesePractise, then check.

📝 Exam tips

  • Learn the 25 written answers (Q1–Q25) word for word: they are the biggest part of the exam. Use the Answer Trainer: ten a day.
  • Look for the keyword in each question (in yellow in this guide). It tells you which answer to write: "HTML tags" is not the same answer as "HTML", and "script mode" is not "Interactive Mode".
  • Write the key phrases (in green): they are what the teacher looks for. Numbered answers (Q3, Q9, Q12, Q21) need every item.
  • Tick the correct option: read all three options first. "Not" questions (A3, A6, A8, A10) want the odd one out.
  • True or false: one wrong word makes a sentence false: "CSS creates web pages" (F), "Gradient darkens" (F), "Filters select" (F).

Part 1 · Web pages with HTML

Lesson 1 · What is HTML?

The big ideaHTML (Hypertext Markup Language) is the language web pages are written in. It was developed in 1990 by the scientist Tim Berners-Lee. An HTML file is just plain text, so you can type it in Notepad and open it in any web browser.
Key words HTML web page World Wide Web hyperlink W3C HTML editor text editor web browser
🗒️ index.html - Notepad
<HTML>
 <BODY>
  Hello, world!
 </BODY>
</HTML>
1. Type the HTML in a text editor and save it as .html
🌐 Microsoft Edge
Hello, world!
2. Double-click the file, or open Edge and press Ctrl + O

Written questions (learn these answers)

Q1What do you know about HTML?

HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language. It was developed in the year 1990 by the scientist Tim Berners-Lee.

💡 Hey Tim, Make Links! Tim Berners-Lee, 1990.
Q2What's the use of HTML?

HTML is mainly used to create web pages that are displayed on the World Wide Web. Each page contains a series of connections to other pages called hyperlinks.

💡 Think of the spider: HTML makes the pages 📄, hyperlinks join them into the web 🕸️.
Q3Write any three features of HTML 5?
  1. HTML documents are simple text files.
  2. HTML is not a case sensitive language.
  3. HTML has many tags to make web pages.
💡 Three features: Text, Case, Tags. Picture a text file in a suitcase covered in tags! 🧳
Q4Define HTML Editors and Text Editors.

We can create an HTML document using an HTML editor or any text editor.

HTML editors are Adobe Dreamweaver, UltraEdit, TextMate.

Text editors are Notepad, Notepad++.

We can create our HTML documents using Notepad.

💡 Fancy editors have fancy names (Dreamweaver, UltraEdit, TextMate). Plain text editors have plain names: Notepad! 🗒️
Q5How can we view the HTML document?

After creating and saving an HTML document we can view it by double clicking on the HTML document.

We can also open an HTML file by opening Microsoft Edge by clicking on its icon on the desktop or the taskbar and then pressing Control + O keys.

💡 Two ways to view: double-click the file 🖱️🖱️, or open Edge and press Ctrl + O (O for Open).
⚠️ Watch outNotepad is a text editor; Dreamweaver, UltraEdit and TextMate are HTML editors. Don't swap them. W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) sets the rules for the web; it is not a program.

Part 1 · Web pages with HTML

Lesson 2 · HTML tags and page structure

The big ideaTags are the instructions of HTML. Each tag sits inside angular brackets < >. Most tags come in pairs: an opening tag like <BODY> and a closing tag with a slash like </BODY>; these are container tags. Every page has the same skeleton: HTML on the outside, then HEAD, then BODY.
Key words tag angular brackets < > opening tag closing tag container tag HEAD BODY
<HTML>
<HEAD> the title and styles </HEAD>
<BODY> what you see on the page </BODY>
</HTML>
The page skeleton: boxes inside a box
<P>
opening tag
</P>
closing tag: the slash / closes
< is "less than", > is "greater than": together, angular brackets

From your worksheet

#Tick the correct option
A1
Which of the following is the correct structure of HTML tags?
(a) <HTML> <HTML> </HEAD> <HEAD> </BODY> </BODY> (b) <HTML> </HTML> <HEAD> </HEAD> <BODY> </BODY> ✔ (c) <HTML> <HEAD> </HEAD> <BODY> </BODY> </HTML>

Written questions (learn these answers)

Q6What do you know about HTML tags?

Tags are elements that are used to specify the structure of an HTML document. HTML tags begin with the less than character (<) and end with the greater than symbol (>), which are called angular brackets.

💡 A tag is a word in a pointy sandwich 🥪: < (Less than) at the start, > (Greater than) at the end. Both together are angular brackets: they have angles! 📐
Q7What is the difference between opening and closing tags?

In HTML, most tags have an opening and a closing tag. For example <HTML> is the opening tag and </HTML> is the closing tag. The tags which have both opening and ending tags are called container tags.

💡 The closing tag has a /: a door shutting 🚪. A box with a top and a bottom holds things inside: a container 📦. Both tags = container tags.
💡 Memory trickH-H-B-H: open HTML, then HEAD (open and close), then BODY (open and close), and close HTML last. The head comes before the body, like on you! 🙂
⚠️ Watch outIn A1, option (b) closes HTML straight away, so HEAD and BODY end up outside the page. </HTML> is always the very last tag. The slash goes at the start: </BODY>, not <BODY/>.

The big ideaThe <IMG> tag adds a picture to a web page. Its attributes give extra details: src (which picture file), alt (the alternate text shown if the picture can't be displayed), height and width. Pictures can be .jpg, .gif, .png or .bmp files.

If the picture can't load, the alt text is shown

Lesson 4 · Links: internal, external and URLs

The big ideaA link (hyperlink) takes you to another page when you click it. There are two types of linking: internal and external. The address of a page is its URL: an absolute URL is the complete address; a relative URL is a short one. The target attribute says where the link opens, and link, alink and vlink set link colours.
Key words link (hyperlink) internal linking external linking URL absolute URL relative URL target link · alink · vlink
https://www.myschool.com/pages/news.html
howthe websitethe folderthe file
An absolute URL has every part: the complete path. A relative URL is just the end, e.g. news.html.
Attribute (in <BODY>)Colours…
linklinks not clicked yet
alinkactive links (being clicked)
vlinkvisited links
<A href="news.html" target="_blank">News</A>
target="_blank" opens the link in a new tab

Part 2 · Styling with CSS

Lesson 5 · What is CSS?

The big ideaCSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. HTML builds the page; CSS styles it: colours, fonts, sizes and positions. CSS does not create pages. A CSS file is saved with a .css extension, and one file can style a whole website, so large websites are easy to format.
Key words CSS Cascading Style Sheets style selector property value .css
h1 { color: blue; }
selector
which elementsproperty
what to changevalue
change it to what
A CSS rule has three parts: selector, property and value. "Make every h1 heading blue."

Q8What do you know about CSS?

CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. CSS is used to style HTML pages and it's used to specify how HTML elements are displayed.

💡 HTML builds the house 🏠, CSS paints and decorates it 🎨. A cascade is a waterfall: the styles flow down onto every page.

Part 2 · Styling with CSS

Lesson 6 · Three kinds of style sheet

The big ideaThere are three types of CSS: inline (a style attribute inside one tag, for a single element), internal (a <STYLE> block in the head section, for one page) and external (a separate .css file, for many pages). Properties like font-family, text-indent and background-position do the styling.
Key words inline internal external style attribute head section font-family text-indent background-position

1 · Inline

<P style="color:red">Hi</P>

In one tag: styles a single element with the style attribute.

2 · Internal

<HEAD>
 <STYLE>
  p {color:red}
 </STYLE>
</HEAD>

In the head section: styles one page.

3 · External

📄 style.css
p {color:red}

In a separate .css file: styles many pages.

PropertyWhat it doesExample
font-familysets the font of the textfont-family: Arial;
text-indentindents the first line of texttext-indent: 30px;
background-imageputs a picture behind the pagebackground-image: url("sky.jpg");
background-positionsets the position of that imagebackground-position: center;

Part 3 · Programming and Python

Lesson 7 · Programs and programming languages

The big ideaA program is a sequence of instructions that tells the computer how to do a particular task. Programs are written in programming languages, and writing them is called programming. There are three main types of language: machine, assembly and high level. A computer only understands machine language, so a translator (a compiler or an interpreter) converts high level code into machine code.
Key words program programming programming language machine language assembly language high level language translator compiler interpreter
3 · High level print("Hi")almost English: easy for people
2 · Assembly level MOV A, 5short code words
1 · Machine level 10110000 0101only 0s and 1s: what the computer understands
The three types of programming language
print("Hi")high level code
➜ 🗣️ translator ➜compiler or interpreter
0101 1100machine code
CompilerInterpreter
translates the whole program in one gotranslates and runs it one line at a time (Python uses one)

This lesson has no tick, blank or true/false questions on the worksheet: just the three written answers below.

Written questions (learn these answers)

Q11What do you know about computer programming?

A sequence of instructions given to the computer to perform a particular task is called a program. These programs are created using programming languages. The process of creating a program is also known as programming.

💡 A program is a recipe 📋: a sequence of instructions for one task. The language you write it in is a programming language; writing it is programming.
Q12Write the names of types of computer programming languages?

There are three main types:

  1. Machine level language
  2. Assembly level language
  3. High level language
💡 Climb the ladder 🪜: Machine (0s and 1s), Assembly (short codes), High (almost English). M-A-H: "Ma, help!"
Q13Describe a language translator?

A language translator such as a compiler or interpreter is needed to convert the high level language code into machine code. A computer understands only machine language.

💡 A translator turns High into Machine 🗣️➡️0101. Its two names: Compiler and Interpreter, "Can I translate?"
⚠️ Watch outA computer understands only machine language, never high level code directly. Spell it Assembly (not "assemble") and say "level language" for all three types.
✏️ Try these (answers at the back)

  2. Name the two kinds of language translator.
  3. What is the process of creating a program called?

Part 3 · Programming and Python

Lesson 8 · Meet Python: interactive and script mode

The big ideaPython is a high level programming language with simple syntax, so it is easy to read and write. It was developed in 1991 in the Netherlands. You can use it in two ways: interactive mode (type a line, press Enter, see the answer at once) or script mode (write a long program in the editor and save it as a .py file). IDLE is the program that comes with Python.
Key words Python syntax Object Oriented reusable code interactive mode script mode .py IDLE
🐍 IDLE Shell (interactive mode)
>>> print("Hello")
Hello
>>> 5 + 3
8
Type, press Enter, get the output straight away
📄 game.py (script mode)
# my program
name = "Sara"
print("Hi", name)
print("Let's play!")
Write many lines, save as .py, then Run
💬 Interactive mode🎬 Script mode
Wherethe Python shell (the >>> prompt)the Python editor (IDLE)
Outputstraight after you press Enterwhen you run the program
Best forvery short lines of codelong programs with multiple lines
Save?noyes, as a .py file you can edit

Written questions (learn these answers)

Q14What do you know about Python?

Python is a high level programming language. It has simple syntax which makes it easy to read and write. It was developed in 1991 at the National Research Institute for Mathematics and Computer Science in the Netherlands.

💡 Python 🐍 hatched in 1991 (one year after HTML's 1990) in the Netherlands 🇳🇱 (think tulips 🌷). Simple syntax = easy to read and write.
Q15Write any 2 features of Python?

Python is easy to learn and use as compared to other programming languages.

Python can perform complex tasks using less code.

💡 Easy in, little out: easy to learn and use; less code for complex tasks. ✌️
Q16What is an Object Oriented procedure?

Python supports Object Oriented procedure. An Object Oriented procedure helps the programmer to write reusable code and develop applications using less code as compared to other programming languages.

💡 Object Oriented = LEGO bricks 🧱: build a brick once and reuse it everywhere, so you build apps with less code.
Q17Describe Interactive Mode of Python while writing a code.

In the Interactive Mode when we type a command and press Enter, in the very next step we get the output. Interactive Mode is very convenient for writing very short lines of code.

💡 Interactive = chatting 💬: you type, press Enter, and Python answers straight away. Chats are short, so it suits short lines.
Q18Describe the script mode of Python language.

To write long Python codes or programs having multiple lines, script mode is the appropriate way. In this mode the code is written in the Python editor and saved with a ".py" extension. In this mode we can save and edit the file.

💡 A script is a film script 🎬: long, many lines, written down and saved (as .py) so you can edit it later.
Q19What do you know about Python IDLE?

The installer for Windows installs an IDLE module by default. IDLE is an acronym for Integrated Development and Learning Environment. It is used in script mode for creating, editing and executing Python programs.

💡 IDLE is never idle! It Integrates, Develops, Learns in an Environment, and it Creates, Edits and Executes scripts (C, E, E).
⚠️ Watch outPython is 1991, HTML is 1990: don't swap them. Python files end in .py (not .python), CSS files in .css. IDLE is Integrated Development and Learning Environment.

Lesson 9 · GIMP painting tools

The big ideaGIMP is a free program for drawing, painting and changing pictures. It has a large variety of painting tools, each with its own job: fill an area, mix two colours, paint soft strokes, draw sharp lines, or rub colour out.

Painting toolIts job

✏️Pencildraws freehand lines with hard edges
💨Airbrushsprays soft colour, like a spray can
🖋️Inkdraws like a calligraphic ink pen
🧽Eraserremoves areas of colour from an image or a selected part
Paintbrush: fuzzy edge
Pencil: hard edge
Gradient: two colours mixed

Written questions (learn these answers)

Q20Why do we use GIMP for drawing?

There are a large variety of painting tools in GIMP which can be used to paint our drawings beautifully. These tools can also be used to draw, paint and modify images.

💡 GIMP is a giant art box 🎨: lots of painting tools to draw, paint and modify. D-P-M: "Draw Pretty Masterpieces".
Q21Enlist the names of some common tools used for drawings in GIMP?
  1. The bucket fill tool (fills colour in an area)
  2. Gradient tool
  3. Paintbrush tool
  4. Pencil tool
  5. Eraser tool
💡 Big Green Pencils Paint Easily: Bucket fill 🪣, Gradient 🌈, Paintbrush 🖌️, Pencil ✏️, Eraser 🧽.
Q22Why do we use the paintbrush tool in GIMP?

The paintbrush tool allows us to paint using fuzzy brush strokes. All strokes are rendered using the currently selected brush type.

💡 A paintbrush is soft and fuzzy 🖌️ like a fluffy tail. Every stroke uses the brush you selected.
Q23What is the use of the pencil tool in drawing?

The pencil tool is used to draw free-hand lines having hard edges. It is similar to the paintbrush tool but the pencil tool does not produce fuzzy edges.

💡 A pencil has a sharp point ✏️, so its lines have hard edges. The brush is the fuzzy one; the pencil is not.
Q24Is the Eraser tool important while drawing in GIMP?

The eraser tool is a very important tool for drawing because it is used to remove areas of colour from an image or the selected part of an image.

💡 Everyone makes mistakes, so yes, it's very important 🧽: it removes areas of colour from the image or the selected part.
⚠️ Watch outShear is a transform tool (it slants a picture), not a painting tool. Gradient mixes colours; it does not darken. Paintbrush = fuzzy, pencil = hard edges.

original

Q25What is the use of the clone tool in GIMP?

In GIMP the clone tool reproduces the selected parts in an image. It copies the selected parts of the image and pastes them in any other part of the image.

💡 A clone is an identical twin 🐑🐑: the clone tool copies the selected part and pastes it somewhere else in the same image.
💡 Memory trickDodge = Daylight ☀️ (lighter); Burn = Black toast 🍞 (darker). Heal heals a scratch like a plaster 🩹. Filters = Fun effects ✨.
⚠️ Watch outOnly Clone copies (A11 is not "Both": Dodge just lightens). Filters do not select (C13 is False). Contiguous means "touching": Fuzzy Select picks touching areas of a similar colour.

Cheat sheet

🌐 HTML

Hypertext Markup Language · Tim Berners-Lee, 1990 · W3C sets web standards · text file, not case sensitive, many tags · HTML editors: Dreamweaver, UltraEdit, TextMate · text editors: Notepad, Notepad++ · view: double-click, or Edge + Ctrl + O

🏷️ Tags

inside angular brackets < > · opening <HTML>, closing </HTML> · both = container tags · order: HTML › HEAD › /HEAD › BODY › /BODY › /HTML

🖼️ Pictures

<IMG> adds a picture · attributes: src, alt (alternate text), height, width · formats: .jpg .gif .png .bmp · .xlsx is not a picture · target is not an IMG attribute

🔗 Links

types: internal and external (both) · target = where a link opens · absolute URL = complete path · colours: link, alink (active), vlink (visited) · C7: write T

🎨 CSS

Cascading Style Sheets · styles pages, does not create them · easy to format large websites · rule = selector, property, value · saved as .css · selectors pick HTML elements

📑 Style sheets

inline (style attribute, one element) · internal (in the head section) · external (separate .css file) · NOT "inside" · font-family = font · text-indent = first line · background-position = image position

🤖 Programs

program = sequence of instructions for a task · programming = creating programs · types: machine, assembly, high level · translator: compiler or interpreter → machine code · computer understands only machine language

🐍 Python

high level, simple syntax · 1991, Netherlands · easy to learn, less code · Object Oriented → reusable code · interactive: Enter → output now, short code · script: long code, editor, .py, save and edit · IDLE = Integrated Development and Learning Environment

🖌️ Painting tools

🪣 bucket fill · 🌈 gradient = mix of two colours (not darken) · 🖌️ paintbrush = fuzzy, freehand · ✏️ pencil = hard edges · 💨 airbrush · 🖋️ ink = calligraphic pen · 🧽 eraser removes colour · Shear is not a painting tool

🪄 Fixing tools

🐑 clone copies a part · 🩹 heal removes defects · ☀️ dodge lightens · 🔥 burn darkens · 🪄 fuzzy select = similar colour areas · ✨ filters = special effects (they don't select)

All 25 model answers

The keyword tells you which answer to write. The key phrases score the marks. Cover the answer, write it on paper, then check.

Q1What do you know about HTML?

HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language. It was developed in the year 1990 by the scientist Tim Berners-Lee.

Q2What's the use of HTML?

HTML is mainly used to create web pages that are displayed on the World Wide Web. Each page contains a series of connections to other pages called hyperlinks.

Q3Write any three features of HTML 5?
  1. HTML documents are simple text files.
  2. HTML is not a case sensitive language.
  3. HTML has many tags to make web pages.
Q4Define HTML Editors and Text Editors.

We can create an HTML document using an HTML editor or any text editor.

HTML editors are Adobe Dreamweaver, UltraEdit, TextMate.

Text editors are Notepad, Notepad++.

We can create our HTML documents using Notepad.

Q5How can we view the HTML document?

After creating and saving an HTML document we can view it by double clicking on the HTML document.

We can also open an HTML file by opening Microsoft Edge by clicking on its icon on the desktop or the taskbar and then pressing Control + O keys.

Q6What do you know about HTML tags?

Tags are elements that are used to specify the structure of an HTML document. HTML tags begin with the less than character (<) and end with the greater than symbol (>), which are called angular brackets.

Q7What is the difference between opening and closing tags?

In HTML, most tags have an opening and a closing tag. For example <HTML> is the opening tag and </HTML> is the closing tag. The tags which have both opening and ending tags are called container tags.

Q8What do you know about CSS?

CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. CSS is used to style HTML pages and it's used to specify how HTML elements are displayed.

Q9List down the different types of CSS?
  1. Inline style sheet
  2. Internal style sheet
  3. External style sheet
Q10Define inline style sheet.

The inline style sheet is used to apply the style to a single HTML element using the style attribute.

Q11What do you know about computer programming?

A sequence of instructions given to the computer to perform a particular task is called a program. These programs are created using programming languages. The process of creating a program is also known as programming.

Q12Write the names of types of computer programming languages?

There are three main types:

  1. Machine level language
  2. Assembly level language
  3. High level language
Q13Describe a language translator?

A language translator such as a compiler or interpreter is needed to convert the high level language code into machine code. A computer understands only machine language.

Q14What do you know about Python?

Python is a high level programming language. It has simple syntax which makes it easy to read and write. It was developed in 1991 at the National Research Institute for Mathematics and Computer Science in the Netherlands.

Q15Write any 2 features of Python?

Python is easy to learn and use as compared to other programming languages.

Python can perform complex tasks using less code.

Q16What is an Object Oriented procedure?

Python supports Object Oriented procedure. An Object Oriented procedure helps the programmer to write reusable code and develop applications using less code as compared to other programming languages.

Q17Describe Interactive Mode of Python while writing a code.

In the Interactive Mode when we type a command and press Enter, in the very next step we get the output. Interactive Mode is very convenient for writing very short lines of code.

Q18Describe the script mode of Python language.

To write long Python codes or programs having multiple lines, script mode is the appropriate way. In this mode the code is written in the Python editor and saved with a ".py" extension. In this mode we can save and edit the file.

Q19What do you know about Python IDLE?

The installer for Windows installs an IDLE module by default. IDLE is an acronym for Integrated Development and Learning Environment. It is used in script mode for creating, editing and executing Python programs.

Q20Why do we use GIMP for drawing?

There are a large variety of painting tools in GIMP which can be used to paint our drawings beautifully. These tools can also be used to draw, paint and modify images.

Q21Enlist the names of some common tools used for drawings in GIMP?
  1. The bucket fill tool (fills colour in an area)
  2. Gradient tool
  3. Paintbrush tool
  4. Pencil tool
  5. Eraser tool
Q22Why do we use the paintbrush tool in GIMP?

The paintbrush tool allows us to paint using fuzzy brush strokes. All strokes are rendered using the currently selected brush type.

Q23What is the use of the pencil tool in drawing?

The pencil tool is used to draw free-hand lines having hard edges. It is similar to the paintbrush tool but the pencil tool does not produce fuzzy edges.

Q24Is the Eraser tool important while drawing in GIMP?

The eraser tool is a very important tool for drawing because it is used to remove areas of colour from an image or the selected part of an image.

Q25What is the use of the clone tool in GIMP?

In GIMP the clone tool reproduces the selected parts in an image. It copies the selected parts of the image and pastes them in any other part of the image.
